answer:
**Best estimate:** **8,200,000 retail units** of **Coca-Cola** sold in the **CSD/carbonates category** in **Danish retail/off-trade** in **January 2026**.

**Range:** **6,000,000–11,000,000 units**  
**Confidence:** **Low-to-moderate (~35%)**, mainly because “units” depends heavily on whether multipacks count as one retail unit or as individual cans/bottles, and because brand-level Danish retail scanner data is not public.

**Assumptions used:**
- Interpreting **units** as **retail selling units/packages scanned at checkout**: e.g., one 1.5L bottle = 1 unit; one 6-pack = 1 unit.
- Danish off-trade soft-drink volume is large: a DTU report using Euromonitor data says Danish **retail/off-trade soft-drink sales** were about **86% of total soft-drink sales**, and that soda/carbonates off-trade was about **80% of total soda/carbonates**; the same report gives 2025 total soft-drink sales at **966 million litres**. ([food.dtu.dk](https://www.food.dtu.dk/-/media/institutter/foedevareinstituttet/publikationer/pub-2025/markeds-og-vareundersoegelse-af-energidrikke-i-danmark-final-report.pdf))
- I estimate annual Danish off-trade carbonates at roughly **475–500 million litres**, Coca-Cola-brand share at roughly **23–28%** after the 2025 anti-US-brand effect, and January seasonality at about **6.5–7.5%** of annual volume.
- Carlsberg bottles/distributes Coca-Cola in Denmark, and in 2025 it said Danish Coca-Cola volumes were “slightly down” amid a boycott effect, while local cola brands gained share; however, in Q1 2026 Carlsberg said the Coke portfolio in Denmark/Finland was again providing growth, so I did not apply a large continuing collapse assumption. ([investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/danes-boycotting-us-products-like-cocacola-carlsberg-says-4010792?utm_source=openai))
- Converted litres to retail units using an average of about **1.0–1.2 litres per scanned selling unit**, reflecting a mix of 1.5L bottles, 0.5L bottles, and multipacks.

FORECAST=8200000
